opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. Since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, full-time employees may have admin. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Anita Young (E001) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on Anita's employment type: HR note says full_time (Payroll Specialist, recommending admin), while the Security note says contractor with basic security training, recommending read. Given the conflict and the policy that contractors may never have admin (and basic training limits contractors to read), the Security record is the more restrictive and safer basis. Requested admin exceeds the contractor maximum, so the maximum allowed level is read.
